chain.label: No regulatory framework or effective FAA/company safety oversight of parachute jump operations
chain.trigger: even though FAA inspectors accomplished the inspections of OPC that the agency required, those inspections were insufficient for ensuring the safety of this commercial passenger-carrying operation

chain.label: Pilot's initial and company training left him without proficiency in the Beech King Air
chain.trigger: the pilot's initial training did not provide him with adequate experience and proficiency for Beech King Air operations; the Beech King Air 65-A90 flight training that OPC provided to new company pilots was insufficient

caused_by.evidence: OPC had no structured pilot training program to ensure that company pilots, including the accident pilot, were proficient in the Beech King Air airplane

chain.label: Airplane not properly repaired after 2016 accident and not maintained airworthy
chain.trigger: the accident airplane was not airworthy because (1) it had not been properly repaired after the previous accident and (2) OPC and its contract mechanic did not maintain the airplane in an airworthy condition

caused_by.evidence: OPC did not comply with the airplane manufacturer's inspection program

chain.label: Twisted left wing (leading-edge-up) requiring full left-wing-down aileron trim, reducing stall margin
chain.trigger: the twisted left wing that resulted from the airplane's previous accident reduced the airplane's stall margin, which likely caused the left wing to stall before the right wing

caused_by.evidence: The left wing was not repaired after the July 2016 accident, and the airplane required full left-wing-down aileron trim to fly straight and level

chain.label: Airplane operated near or beyond the aft CG limit with unrestrained occupants
chain.trigger: the airplane was likely operated near or possibly beyond the aft CG limit during the accident takeoff

caused_by.evidence: the method that OPC used to calculate the airplane's CG for each parachute jump flight, including the accident flight, was flawed because it did not include the weights of tandem parachute systems, tandem harnesses, and single parachute systems

chain.label: Pilot elected an intersection takeoff with 4,500 ft remaining instead of the standard full-length departure
chain.trigger: the pilot most likely followed a similar flight trajectory and performed a takeoff from the runway 8 intersection rather than the standard departure location

caused_by.evidence: the pilot might have been overconfident in his abilities to safely operate the King Air airplane in commercial parachute jump operations

chain.label: Aggressive low-altitude high-bank turn with simultaneous pitch-up; pilot overcontrolled the airplane
chain.trigger: the pilot conducted an intentional aggressive takeoff maneuver involving a low-altitude high-bank turn and simultaneous pitch-up maneuver

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's minimal training did not provide him with the necessary experience to fully understand the altered handling qualities of the airplane

the lighter control column forces (due to the airplane's operation near the aft CG limit) could have resulted in an increased airplane pitch response and a subsequently higher AOA when the pilot moved the control column aft
a departure from runway 8 using the intersecting taxiway at midfield would leave 4,500 ft of available runway for takeoff, resulting in rotation farther down the runway and a turn soon thereafter

chain.label: Maneuver flown between about 100 and 200 ft agl, leaving no recovery margin
chain.trigger: caused the airplane to enter an accelerated stall at an altitude between about 100 and 200 ft

caused_by.evidence: when the airplane was about 10 ft off the ground, the airplane 'pulled up and to the left in one motion'

chain.label: Accelerated stall as AOA rapidly exceeded the critical AOA, left wing stalling first
chain.trigger: the pilot's aggressive takeoff maneuver caused an accelerated stall

caused_by.evidence: Because the pilot performed the accident takeoff aggressively, the resulting AOA likely exceeded the stall AOA quickly and with little warning
The higher AOA of the left wing would have resulted in that wing stalling first. Thus, the stall margin for the left wing would have been reduced
an aft CG reduces an airplane's static longitudinal stability... could cause a pilot to overcontrol an airplane

chain.label: Airplane rolled left, went inverted in a 45-degree nose-down attitude; recovery not possible
chain.trigger: a subsequent loss of control at an altitude from which recovery was not possible

caused_by.evidence: A pilot's failure to immediately address an accelerated stall can result in a loss of control
precipitated the airplane's roll to the left
loss of control at an altitude from which recovery was not possible

chain.label: Inverted nose-down impact with terrain 630 ft northeast of the runway, followed by postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted a grass and dirt area about 630 ft northeast of the departure end of the runway, and a postcrash fire ensued

caused_by.evidence: The airplane's orientation and trajectory at the time of impact were consistent with a sharp turn and loss of control

chain.label: Pilot and 10 passengers fatally injured; airplane destroyed
